text: Tools forged from Manifested Ingots: a pickaxe, axe, shovel, blade, shears and hoe. They start diamond-hard with **1,024 durability**.
While they can draw Pulse from a carried cell they spare their edge: every paid action mends a point of wear instead of costing one.
pages.title: Spiritgear tools
Pulse for work
text: A block mined costs **2 Pulse**, a hit **3**, a use **1**, taken from any Pulse Cell you carry.
With no Pulse the tool still works, but it wears like any other tool, and the action bar tells you it is starving.

pages.title: Ranking up
text: Ranks are where Spiritgear becomes something special, and they are meant to take real effort. Seat the piece in the station with its totem nearby, put the **catalysts** in the station's catalyst slots, and keep the Pulse flowing:
- **Echo Attune**, Fire: rank 0 to 1. **45 seconds** at **48 Pulse a second**, and **4 Attuned Echo**.
- **Echo Bind**, Water: rank 1 to 2. **90 seconds** at **64**, and **4 Bound Echo**. Bind refuses rank 0.

- **Echo Manifest**, Spirit: rank 2 to 3. **180 seconds** at **96**, and **2 Resonant Cores** and **4 Loom Thread**. Loom Thread only comes from [The Unsung](the_unsung), so the top rank waits until you have beaten it.
Those figures are before pack settings. The station waits, spending nothing, until its catalysts are in; they are used up when the rank lands. The tooltip always shows what the next rank needs.

pages.title: What ranks give
text: - **Attuned**: every action costs one Pulse less (mining 1, a hit 2, a use 1), mines **20%** faster, and hits harder.
- **Bound**: a starved swing no longer wears the tool, and it mines **45%** faster.
- **Manifested**: mines **80%** faster, half of starved swings even mend a point, and voice perks grow stronger.

The blade and its [weapon family](spiritgear_weapons) gain the most: **+2**, **+5** and **+10** attack damage by rank, and a little attack speed. A Manifested blade hits **bosses 25% harder** and heals you for **10%** of every blow, which is what you want in a long fight.
A Loom-linked pick spends **0 Pulse** to mine. Echo Unweave takes a damaged tool back apart into one Manifested Ingot, forgetting rank and voice.

pages.title: Shears and hoe
text: The **Spiritgear Shears** trim leaves, wool, vines and cobweb, and rank and bind like the rest of the set.
- **Earth**: a swing takes the whole 3x3 face of foliage.  - **Air**: trimming costs no Pulse and no wear at all.
- **Water**: a sheared sheep is left its fleece, always at Manifested.  - **Fire**: used on a beehive it smokes the bees calm, so no swarm.
- **Spirit**: what it shears is mended afterwards, and nearby beasts worth shearing glow.  - **Loom**: the cuttings come straight to hand.
The **Spiritgear Hoe** reaps and sows in one motion: use it on a ripe crop and the harvest drops while one seed goes back into the ground.
- **Earth**: turns a 3x3 of soil at once.  - **Water**: its furrows come out wet, and fields you walk past stay watered.
- **Air**: reaps a 3x3.  - **Loom**: reaps a 5x5 and spends no Pulse doing it.  - **Spirit**: a quarter of harvests come back doubled.

pages.title: A cell of its own
text: Every piece of Spiritgear and Spiritweave, the [Resonance Maul](resonance_maul) and the [Sixfold Staff](sixfold_staff) can carry a **Pulse Cell** of its own. Pick the cell up in your inventory and **right-click it onto the piece**: it goes inside, charge and all.
The piece always spends from its own cell first. Only when that cell is empty does it reach for the cells you carry, so a well-charged set keeps going long after your pockets run dry.

Right-click a bigger cell (a **{item:tribalpower:greater_pulse_cell}** or a **{item:tribalpower:grand_pulse_cell}**) onto a piece holding a smaller one to upgrade it; the old cell comes back to your cursor. A cell of the same size or smaller tops the seated one up instead. The tooltip shows what each piece holds.
Right-click a piece with an **empty cursor** to take its cell back out, charge and all.
